definition: Susan T. Dumais (born August 11, 1953) is an American computer scientist who is a leader in the field of information retrieval, and has been a significant contributor to Microsoft's search technologies.
details: According to Mary Jane Irwin, who heads the Athena Lecture awards committee, "Her sustained contributions have shaped the thinking and direction of human-computer interaction and information retrieval." In 2025, she was elected to the American Philosophical Society.

explainer.lead: Susan Dumais is an American computer scientist (born 1953). Her work spans computer science and information science.

timeline.what: Receives the Tony Kent Strix award
Receives the ACM SIGCHI Lifetime Research Award
